name: Bulleted list
instruction: Present the answer as a bulleted list, one point per bullet, because the person wants points they can scan. Keep any lead-in to one short line.
effect: The body is a bulleted list

name: Numbered list
instruction: Present the answer as a numbered list in order, one step or item per number, because the order matters to the person.
effect: The body is a numbered list

name: Table
instruction: Present the answer as a markdown table with a header row, one row per item and one column per attribute, because the person wants to compare across rows.
effect: Contains a markdown table with a header row

name: Checklist
instruction: Present the answer as a checklist of actionable items, each starting with "- [ ]", because the person will tick them off.

name: Pros and cons
example: Pros and cons of remote work
instruction: Present the answer as two lists, one headed "Pros" and one headed "Cons", because the person wants to weigh both sides. Put the weightiest items first in each.
effect: Two lists headed Pros and Cons

name: One-pager
instruction: Write it as a one-pager: short headed sections that fit on a single page, at most about 450 words, because the person needs something that can be read in one sitting.
effect: Headed sections, at most about 450 words
